evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:1049 — inside `send_payment_reminders`, the per-invoice loop resolves recipients with `let user_ids = self.get_unit_resident_user_ids(invoice.unit_id).await?;`. The `?` propagates any transient DB error for a SINGLE unit out of the whole function, aborting reminder processing for every remaining invoice in the batch for that ~60s tick.

This is inconsistent with the error handling used everywhere else in the same file: the inner notification-send loop (mod.rs:1062-1088) uses `match { Ok(()) => .., Err(e) => { warn!; } }` and never aborts the batch, and the sibling jobs (dispatch_vote_closed_notifications votes.rs:214-245, fire_due_report_schedules mod.rs:1305-1352) all `continue` past a per-item error rather than `?`-aborting. One bad unit's resident lookup should skip that invoice, not the rest.

Impact: LOW / self-healing — invoices already processed earlier in the batch were stamped via `mark_payment_reminder_sent` (mod.rs:1094) so they are not re-sent; invoices after the failing one are simply delayed until the next ~60s tick when the transient error clears. No data loss, no duplicate. It is a robustness/consistency smell: a single unit with (e.g.) an orphaned membership row can repeatedly stall the tail of the reminder batch. Confidence medium: the abort is confirmed by static read; the trigger (a transient/permanent error from get_unit_resident_user_ids) is inferred, not runtime-confirmed. Fix (backend-only): replace the `?` at 1049 with `match { Ok(v) => v, Err(e) => { tracing::warn!(invoice_id=%invoice.id, error=%e, "failed to resolve residents; skipping invoice this tick"); continue; } }` to match the file's prevailing pattern.

Cross-cutting send-then-stamp ordering with no downstream idempotency: the scheduler dispatch jobs send notifications FIRST and stamp the dedup watermark SECOND, so a stamp-write failure after a successful send causes the next ~60s tick to re-send to all recipients. votes.rs:246-285 — `notify_vote_closed(...)` is awaited, then `mark_closed_notified(*vote_id)` is called and, on error, only logs `"next tick may resend"` (votes.rs:278-285). Same shape in send_payment_reminders mod.rs:1062-1101 (`notify_payment_due` per user, then `mark_payment_reminder_sent`, error logged `"next tick may resend"`) and dispatch_announcement_notifications / dispatch_vote_started_notifications.

The individual notify_* calls carry no idempotency key that would let a repeat delivery be de-duplicated downstream (contrast: CreateFault in voice_commands.rs threads an `idempotency_key`, and the OAuth/notification pipelines elsewhere do dedup). So a resend is a genuine duplicate push/email, not a downstream no-op. For payment reminders this means duplicate dunning emails to residents; for vote-closed it means duplicate result notifications to every participant.

Impact: LOW and narrow — it only triggers when the notification transport succeeds but the immediately-following watermark UPDATE fails (a small DB-failure window), and the behaviour is an explicitly-acknowledged at-least-once tradeoff (in-code comments say "next tick may resend"). Filed as a signal because the mitigation is real and unimplemented: thread a deterministic idempotency key (e.g. notification_type + vote_id/invoice_id + user_id) through notify_* so a resend collapses at the delivery layer, upgrading the pattern from at-least-once to effectively-once. Confidence medium (static; failure path not runtime-forced). No fix asserted beyond the idempotency-key direction; this is a hardening backlog item, not a crash/security bug.
